correctness.rationale: The 15-vertex line graph of Petersen has 30 edges and at most one common neighbor for any two vertices. Its Lovasz neighborhood complex is the nerve of an S5-invariant cover of the 30-vertex,60-edge bipartite double cover by contractible left stars with singleton intersections; the equivariant nerve theorem identifies integral H1 with the rank-31 cycle lattice. A spanning tree has 29 edges, giving 31 integral chord cycles. The two generators (transposition and 5-cycle) act by exact integral matrices; Smith reduction of [As-I | At-I] has 29 invariant units and two twos. The original script verifies full integral unimodular reductions; independently reconstructed the graph, integral cycle basis, 31x62 presentation, and SymPy Smith form, obtaining exactly (Z/2)^2. The seven-class rational character from signed Lefschetz agrees with the dimension 31 and zero trivial multiplicity; finite character values were checked in provided source.
residual_risks: Group-equivariant nerve theorem applies to a cover; integral coinvariant computation independently repeated, though the full separate 120 signed simplex trace code was reviewed rather than executed.

evidence: Square-free/graph-like neighborhood homotopy theorems determine wedge31 S1 nonequivariantly. Shukla concerns degree≤3 or four-regular circulants, not this natural S5 integral action.
